Pin totals: unit 10 packages / 32 files / 1257 tests, 0 failed (rest 85, metadata-protocol 321, metadata-core 47, plugin-audit 58, runtime 240, mcp 304, plugin-auth 160 incl. A4's two named files, objectql 10, spec 7, service-analytics 25); dogfood 9 files / 67 tests, 0 failed; extra corroborating packages/mcp src/mcp-action-tools.test.ts 25/0. Deviations: vitest 4.1.12 rejects `--poolOptions.forks.maxForks` (ran `--maxWorkers=2`); the one-run dogfood batch was OOM-killed twice by the shared memory cgroup (maxWorkers 2, then 1; dmesg "Memory cgroup out of memory") and the first plugin-auth run once, so plugin-auth was re-run as one batch and dogfood ran one file per invocation, sequentially (9 runs, all first-attempt green). No release blocker in any clause; one probe finding (F-probe-3, admin_full_access self-lockout) is flagged for PM triage. No security finding.

### access-security.public-form-withdrawal-layers (rev 5) — PASS
pins: packages/qa/dogfood showcase-public-form-withdrawal-layers.dogfood.test.ts → 4/0 (HTTP, in-process Hono on a booted showcase with an organization active; scores A0, A1, N0, N1 per the ref) · packages/rest src/public-form-withdrawal.test.ts (rest batch 85/0; RestServer over a mocked protocol — the unit layer A2/A3's test oracle names) · packages/metadata-protocol src/protocol.org-scoped-write-refused.test.ts (metadata-protocol batch 321/0; in-process protocol over a stub registry) · packages/metadata-core src/anonymous-form-intake.test.ts 47/0 (unit)

Anonymous probe = curl with no cookie jar and no Authorization header (bin/probe-form.sh): GET /api/v1/forms/contact-us, POST …/submit {name MARKER, email, message}, then the admin's GET /data/showcase_inquiry?name=MARKER. ORG = org_mwet1a40xl7sqk8n (session.activeOrganizationId of the seeded admin)
| # | clause (short) | verdict | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| A0 | org-active admin save is env-wide; withdrawal closes both doors, no row | pass | baseline probe (stock, open): GET 200, POST 201, 1 row. Body = GET /meta/view/showcase_inquiry.contact minus `_*` keys, config.sharing.allowAnonymous false, publicLink kept. With ORG active: the step's literal package-less PUT → 403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE naming the pair (ADR-0146 D11 — see N2 / Parked); the pair save (POST /packages/com.example.showcase/ensure-customization 201, then PUT …?package=com.example.showcase.custom with overrides {package com.example.showcase, basedOn 0.1.0}) → 200 "Saved customization overlay (env-wide, package=com.example.showcase.custom, state=active) …" — env-wide, no org. Probe: GET 404 FORM_NOT_FOUND, POST 404 FORM_NOT_FOUND "No public form configured at /forms/contact-us", 0 rows for the marker. set-active null (200, session org null) → GET /meta/view/showcase_inquiry.contact serves sharing {enabled true, publicLink /forms/contact-us, allowAnonymous false}; set-active ORG again (200). Dogfood pin (same pair route) green |
| A1 | open env-wide: both doors accept; row lands in ORG | pass | with ORG active, pair save allowAnonymous true → 200 (seq 2, env-wide); probe ×2: GET 200, POST 201, 1 row each, organization_id org_mwet1a40xl7sqk8n = ORG |
| A2 | only an explicit false withdraws ([test]) | pass | rest public-form-withdrawal.test.ts + metadata-core anonymous-form-intake.test.ts green (cases named in verify are in those files); no stock fixture (knownGaps) — verdict rests on the pins |
| A3 | any package's withdrawal of the name closes every package's form ([test]) | pass | rest kill-switch describe + metadata-protocol 'two packages shipping a view name' green; verdict rests on the pins |
| A4 | a package's shipped false withdraws ([test]) | pass | metadata-core schema-parsed-false case + metadata-protocol block (a) green; verdict rests on the pins |
| A5 | the package-less env-wide copy is the switch over a closed shipped form ([test]) | pass | metadata-protocol block (c) green; verdict rests on the pins |
| N0 | 200/201 or a row after the withdrawal | pass | 404/404, 0 rows (A0) |
| N1 | save names org=ORG / no-org read still open | pass | save message "env-wide, package=com.example.showcase.custom", no org; no-org read allowAnonymous false (A0) |
| N2 | a 403 to the step-4/5 save | pass | the save the pin makes (pair route) → 200 both times. The literal package-less PUT the steps describe → 403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE, and its message names the package pair ("'view/showcase_inquiry.contact' ships in 'com.example.showcase': save it into 'com.example.showcase.custom' …"), never an organization — the ADR-0146 D11 refusal RUNNER.md's environment facts document, not the organization-scoped refusal this negative guards. Stale step wording → Parked |
| N3 | a door probed with admin credentials | pass | every door call was anonymous (no jar, no header) |
| N4 | A2–A5 scored from the stock boot | pass | scored from the pins only |
| N5 | an org-scoped metadata row met | pass | none: GET /data/sys_metadata?name=showcase_inquiry.contact → 1 row, package com.example.showcase.custom, no organization column |
Probe (~3 min, anonymous + admin): unknown slug → 404 FORM_NOT_FOUND; /forms/ → 404 ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND; submit without email → 400 VALIDATION_FAILED fields[email]; submit carrying owner_id + organization_id 'org_other' → 201, row landed with owner_id null and organization_id = ORG (forged keys ignored); pair save with sharing.enabled false → both doors 404; re-open → 200/201. No finding.

### 1. api-backend.automation-namespace-address · A8 — product defect (low)
Repro: scratch-pair boot (stock showcase + any installed namespace, e.g. qa_b), as admin: `DELETE /api/v1/automation/showcase/showcase_batch_reminders/runs` (no body). Expected per A8/ADR-0150 D5: the automation domain's 405, `Allow: GET` (automationRouteAllow), dispatcher envelope `{success:false,error:{code:METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED,message:"Method not allowed",httpStatus:405}}`, which is the answer the bare `/automation/showcase_batch_reminders/runs` gives. Actual: the Hono transport's 405, `Allow: GET, HEAD`, envelope `{success:false,error:{code,message:"DELETE is not supported for … Allowed: GET, HEAD.",details:{method,path,allowed}}}`. Reproduced twice at 8e3d4a54, as at ee9ad834, with POST and PUT the same. GET on `/automation/showcase/X/trigger` and `/automation/trigger/showcase/X` shows the same split against bare `/X/trigger`. Traps ruled out: dispatcher-vs-hono-route (this is the trap itself, observed on the live Hono mount); wrong-persona (admin); eventual-consistency (n/a). Disposition: product defect (low), unchanged since the prior round. The prior card draft stands; no fix landed between ee9ad834 and 8e3d4a54 (no commit in that range touches automation-address.ts or the every-verb test). Ruling note for the PM: the transport's Allow is not false (HEAD is served, 200, on both the addressed and the bare path), so the harm is two envelopes and two Allow lists for one served shape. A ruling may instead re-spell A8.
Card draft — **"An addressed /automation/:ns/:name/(runs|trigger) under an unserved verb answers the transport's 405 (Allow: GET, HEAD, details envelope), not the automation domain's 405 the bare path gives"**. On a boot with any installed namespace, `DELETE /api/v1/automation/showcase/showcase_batch_reminders/runs` answers 405 `Allow: GET, HEAD` with the transport's `details` envelope. The bare `DELETE /api/v1/automation/showcase_batch_reminders/runs` answers the domain's 405 `Allow: GET` with `httpStatus`. ADR-0150 D5 says an address is served exactly as the bare path. Likely cause: the dispatcher's every-verb declaration (#24228) covers only the two-segment /automation patterns, so the three-segment addressed mounts fall through to Hono's method-not-allowed. Fix: extend the declaration to the addressed shapes, and pin one 3-segment row in automation-every-verb.hono.integration.test.ts. ## Fails

No clause failed. One product defect found by a probe beside the clauses (rule 8), so no item verdict moves on it:

**F1 · api-backend.package-rest-lifecycle · observed beside the clauses — an overwrite re-install is not what the next boot serves**
- Repro rule (scratch app copy, fresh file DB, admin bearer; reproduced on pkg-repro1.db and pkg-repro2.db, plus first seen on pkg.db):
  1. `POST /api/v1/packages?overwrite=false {manifest:{id:"com.example.qa-rollback",name:"…",version:"1.0.0",scope:"project",type:"app"}}` → 201
  2. ≥1 s later, `POST /api/v1/packages?overwrite=true` same id, version "2.0.0" → 201
  3. ≥1 s later, `POST /api/v1/packages?overwrite=true` same id, version "1.0.0" (rollback) → 201; `GET /api/v1/packages/com.example.qa-rollback` → version 1.0.0; the list shows 1 row, 1.0.0
  4. restart the server on the same DB → `GET /api/v1/packages/com.example.qa-rollback` → **2.0.0** (list: 1 row, 2.0.0). Expected 1.0.0, the last manifest written and served.
  - Same-second variant: three installs/overwrites 1.0.0 → 2.0.0 → 3.0.0 in under a second serve 3.0.0 live and **1.0.0** after the restart (pkg-repro2). First seen on pkg.db: 2.0.0 then 2.1.0 (body overwrite) within one second, 2.1.0 live, 2.0.0 after the restart.
- Cause (read, not changed): `sys_packages` is keyed `(id, version)` and the boot/list/get "latest" is `ORDER BY created_at DESC` / `MAX(created_at)` (`packages/services/service-package/src/index.ts` get() and list()). `created_at` is second-granular text, and the upsert keeps an existing `(id, version)` row's `created_at` (package-table.ts). So re-installing an existing version never becomes "latest", and same-second rows tie.
- Traps ruled out: own driving (each POST answered 201 and the live GET showed the expected version before the restart); stale dist (scratch copy, same artifact both boots); dispatcher-vs-hono-route (the restart read uses the same GET door that read the right value before). A PATCH that changes no version on a row that is not latest by created_at should be lost the same way (same root cause, not driven).
- Disposition: product defect (durability / data integrity of the package registry). Not a P0 surface. Whether 18.3.0 had it was not measured.
- Card draft: **"Package registry: after a restart the boot serves an older manifest than the last overwrite re-install (rollback or same-second writes)"** — POST /api/v1/packages?overwrite=true onto a version the package already had (e.g. 1.0.0 → 2.0.0 → 1.0.0), or several installs/overwrites within one second, answers 201 and serves the new manifest live. After a restart, GET /api/v1/packages/:id serves a different, older-written manifest (2.0.0 in the rollback case, the first version in the same-second case). sys_packages picks "latest" by second-granular `created_at`, and the upsert keeps an existing (id, version) row's created_at. Expected: the manifest served after a restart equals the last one written and served. Actual: the restart silently reverts it. Repro: the 4 steps above on a fresh DB. `QA-source: #RECORD · api-backend.package-rest-lifecycle · observed beside the clauses`
